sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A creeping, stoloniferous perennial forming a mat of leaves and reaching about 15 cm tall. It prefers moist soil, often in partial shade. Dark-blue flowers are arranged in whorls on an upright stem; the upper lip is reduced and the lower lip is three-lobed. Each flower produces four nutlets. Native from Europe to northern Iran and north-western Africa.

sections.title: Food and safety
sections.text: Kew records food use but does not specify the parts or preparation, so no more detailed culinary claim is justified here. The sources consulted do not establish a particular toxicity.
